_meta: Atomic conditional patterns — one record per line, JSON object. A pattern is a {precondition, action} pair — it says 'if you see X, do Y'. This is finer-grained than a lesson (which is 'here's a fact'). Schema by-example from xalgorix mining (2026-09-07). Fields: id (unique, prefix PAT-<pack-short>-<n>), class (canonical), name (≤60 chars), precondition (one sentence describing the trigger), action (one sentence describing what to do), evidence (path:line pointer), attribution (<pack>#<key>), source_pack (name), added_at (YYYY-MM-DD), confidence (0.0-1.0 optional). Retrieval: brain.sh recall-class <class> surfaces matching patterns first (they're actionable), then lessons (context). Every recall that returns this record logs to brain/telemetry/retrievals.jsonl.

name: Independent verifier before shipping any finding
precondition: A candidate finding is about to be added to a report OR marked CONFIRMED
action: Dispatch t3-verifier for adversarial REFUTE first; only post-REFUTE survivors enter the report. Never ship a finding that has not been re-exploited by a fresh session

name: Weak-evidence rejection at report time
precondition: About to write a report finding OR merge candidate findings
action: Enforce references/report-template.md evidence contract — reject findings whose evidence is: (a) a screenshot without HTTP request/response pair, (b) 'could lead to' language without demonstrated impact, (c) a duplicate that adds no new impact vs. the original. Dedup findings that share the same root cause into one

name: Focused engagement — selectable methodology phases
precondition: Operator wants a focused engagement (single vuln class, single system, follow-up on a specific lead)
action: Do NOT run the full 22-phase sweep; pass --families or class-specific hunter dispatch (via references/router.md class table) to constrain scope. Full sweep is expensive; focused runs are cheaper and produce better attribution

name: Skills-as-knowledge-modules — lazy load
precondition: About to load a reference doc, hunter playbook, or pack methodology
action: Use references/router.md's load-on-CLASSIFY asset map — do NOT preload; only pull the specific class-row's docs when that class fires. Prevents context bloat and keeps the harness fast

name: Adaptive throttle — runtime automation controls
precondition: A hunter is about to send burst traffic OR the target has returned 429/WAF/latency spike
action: Honor mad-hunt.md §'Adaptive throttle' ceiling — serial ~1 req/2s baseline; ramp only if last ~20 reqs <300ms with zero 429/challenge; back off (halve concurrency, double delay) on 429/WAF/Retry-After/latency>2s. Block is a PIVOT signal, never a hard stop

name: Cross-module IDOR on modular AI security platforms
precondition: Target detected as AILA-shaped: per-module frontends mounted from /modules/<id>/frontend/ AND module-contributed API routers under /api/modules/<id>/*
action: Enumerate module IDs from the extension registry (/api/platform/modules or the frontend's registry.json). For each module ID, test cross-tenant IDOR: call /api/modules/<other-id>/resource with the current tenant's JWT. Module routers frequently inherit only class-level RBAC checks and miss instance-level authorization

name: Discover origin IP via subdomain scan before WAF-bypass ladder
precondition: Target returns `cf-ray` header OR Cloudflare interstitial (challenge-page, Turnstile, 403 with cf-ray)
action: Run CloudRip (packs/CloudRip/cloudrip.py <domain>) against the target's apex + wildcard-discovered subdomains BEFORE burning cycles on the WAF-bypass ladder. Often a subdomain (dev., staging., api-internal., legacy.) exposes the origin IP directly. Then use `curl --resolve <host>:443:<origin-ip>` to bypass Cloudflare entirely. Complementary to brain/lessons.md#AKAMAI ORIGIN-IP methodology (crt.sh SAN mining) — CloudRip does the subdomain-scan variant

name: grep exploitarium first when target software matches
precondition: About to develop a PoC for a well-known target software OR an assigned CVE lands in scope
action: grep -rli '<target-software>' packs/exploitarium/ AND grep '<cve-id>' packs/exploitarium/cves.md before writing fresh. If a folder matches, cd into it, read README, adapt the existing PoC — bikini's PoCs are complete standalone reproducibles. Saves hours of reinvention. Software coverage as of 2026-09-08: 7zip, anydesk, c-ares, curl, discord, discourse, docker, ffmpeg, firefox, floci, flowise, ghidra, gitea, gogs, imagemagick, ladybird

name: Batch/bulk endpoint auth bypass — inject foreign 'id'
precondition: Target has /api/batch_import, /api/bulk_create, /api/mass_action, /api/import_csv OR any endpoint that loops save() over user-supplied items
action: Single-item CREATE endpoints often sanitize input, but batch loops trust user-supplied 'id' and hit ORM polymorphic save() → cross-tenant UPDATE. Inject the 'id' of a foreign object (other tenant's record) inside the batch payload and check for overwrite. Chain: batch inject → cross-tenant IDOR → data manipulation → P1. Source CVE: CVE-2026-9136 MISP <2.5.38 ShadowAttributesController

name: Unauth UDP listener fuzz with degenerate input
precondition: Target has open UDP port on syslog range (513, 514, 601, 6514, 5140, 5514, 10514, 25226) — often enterprise agents (rsyslog, syslog-ng, SIEM collectors)
action: Fuzz with degenerate payloads: all-NUL (\x00*N), all-0xFF (\xff*N), all-space, single-byte, 60KB max-size. Signed-length trim loops that decrement without a lower bound will underflow into 2-billion-iteration OOB read/write. A supervisor that auto-restarts is NOT a mitigation — sustain via burst-repeat. Chain: unauth UDP → SIGSEGV DoS → CVSS 7.5+ if RCE

name: env.js + short-numeric-ID = scale-BOLA
precondition: Leaked API key found in frontend /env.js /config.js /_next/static/*.js AND API endpoint returns objects with 6-digit sequential IDs (order_id=100001, user_id=200002)
action: Iterate at 0.2s intervals across the ID space at ~5 req/sec (avoid rate-limit trip). 300+ records extracted = Critical (proves systematic data exfil, not one-off). 3 records = 'PoC'; 300 = 'breach'. Chain: key discovery → sequential enum → mass PII exfil → Critical

name: SSO parser/validator desync — 'translation gap'
precondition: SAML/OAuth token flow AND the codebase reads a JWT/SAML value TWICE (once for signature validation, once for business logic)
action: Find where the sig validator reads a canonicalized string vs where the DB lookup reads the parsed value. Test with adversarial input: XML-comment injection admin@corp.com<!--x-->.evil.com (sig sees full canonical, DB sees truncated). Same class: JWT jwks-vs-alg header desync, OAuth token-endpoint POST body vs Authorization header desync

name: DNS-rebinding TOCTOU SSRF filter bypass
precondition: SSRF target validates the hostname BEFORE fetching (2-step: resolve+validate, then re-resolve+fetch)
action: Use rbndr.us: <hex_ip1>.<hex_ip2>.rbndr.us alternates between two IPs on each lookup (TTL=0). Example 7f000001.80808080.rbndr.us = 127.0.0.1 ↔ 8.8.8.8. Submit as ?url=http://<rebind>/; server resolves once (8.8.8.8, passes filter), fetches (resolves again → 127.0.0.1, hits IMDS/localhost). For custom payloads: nccgroup/singularity self-hosted rebind server

name: White-box grep-hunt first-pass (finds ~30% of sink bugs)
precondition: About to review a new codebase OR just acquired an ingested repo
action: Run: grep -RnE 'system\(|exec\(|popen\(|eval\(|strcpy\(|strcat\(|memcpy\(|unserialize\(|pickle\.loads|yaml\.load[^_]|Runtime\.getRuntime|Process\.Start|ChildProcess\.exec|shell_exec|passthru|assert\(' <repo>. Follow with: semgrep --config p/security-audit --config p/owasp-top-ten. Any hit needs data-flow tracing to determine exploitability, but the grep prunes the search space from 'entire repo' to '~20 lines of interest'

name: Use secrets-scan.sh wrapper, not raw gitleaks/trufflehog
precondition: About to scan a codebase or file drop for secrets/API keys/tokens
action: Run: bash scripts/secrets-scan.sh <path> [--high-only] [--scanner both]. Wrapper uses pre-generated configs from brain/registry/secrets-rules/ (derived from packs/secrets-patterns-db). --high-only filters to 883 high-confidence patterns (skip low-confidence noise). --verify hits provider APIs to confirm validity (receipt_required). Do NOT run raw gitleaks/trufflehog with default rules — they miss the ReDoS-safe curated subset and produce more false positives

name: Load a Rifteo skill on-demand for capability gaps
precondition: Mission needs a capability mad-hacks doesn't natively cover (AD attack, APK static, clickjacking, HPP, JWT cracking, nuclei template gen, CVE exploit lookup, CVSS scoring)
action: Look up the capability in references/rifteo-skills-catalog.md. If mad-hacks-native column is filled → use ours. If GAP → load packs/rifteo-skills/<skill>/SKILL.md verbatim as a T3 reference for that mission only. Do NOT copy Rifteo content into brain/ — the pack is the SPOT

name: Use dalfox v3 for XSS scan/mining/blind
precondition: About to hand-roll curl loops for XSS parameter mining, reflected/stored/DOM discovery, or blind-XSS at scale
action: Use dalfox v3 recipes from references/dalfox-guide.md. Native --blind-oob feeds interactsh; SARIF/JSONL output stream-parses cleanly; MCP stdio integration enables 6 tool-calls from any MCP-aware runtime. For per-context tuning use brain/payloads/xss-by-context.md + xss-waf-bypass.txt as --custom-payload

name: Study Awesome-Bugbounty-Writeups by class before hunting it
precondition: About to start hunting a specific vuln class you haven't hunted recently OR want to refresh public-disclosure patterns
action: grep the class section in packs/Awesome-Bugbounty-Writeups/README.md, open ~5 top links, note real-world exploitation angles + severity framings. Combines with brain/writeups-corpus.md (full-body distilled corpus) for the complete pre-hunt study

name: Grep Poc pack for Chinese-stack or obscure-CMS targets
precondition: Target has a Chinese-language stack (WeChat mini-program, DingTalk, Baidu Cloud, Chinese enterprise) OR uses an obscure CMS where English writeups return nothing
action: grep packs/Poc/README.md for the CMS/stack keyword, follow the linked upstream (baizesec/bylibrary, EdgeSecurityTeam, pen4uin, etc.) to find PoCs. Adapt to the current target

name: Load a reverse-skill technique on-demand for domain-specific playbooks
precondition: Mission needs a technique-specific playbook: AD attack chain (Kerberoasting, DPAPI, AD CS), cloud metadata path, K8s control plane, container escape, mobile runtime hooking, JWT claim confusion, GraphQL/RPC drift
action: ls packs/reverse-skill/techniques/ then read the matching <technique>.md verbatim as T3 reference for this mission. Cross-reference with packs/rifteo-skills/ for overlap (both cover AD, mobile, container)

name: Grep ai-pentesting for LLM Top 10 techniques
precondition: Hunting an LLM/ML target OR need OWASP LLM Top 10 technique reference beyond the llm-ai-hunter agent
action: grep -r <technique-keyword> packs/ai-pentesting/ — pack has focused prompt-injection, adversarial-ML, model-extraction, jailbreak, RAG-poison technique docs. Cross-load with packs/strix/skills-internal/vulnerabilities/{llm_prompt_injection,agentic_system_security}.md for depth on the same class

name: Load strix skills-internal vulnerability doc for methodology depth
precondition: A vuln-class hunt needs depth beyond brain/lessons.md + CBH's hunt-<class>.md (parser differentials, bypass matrices, IMDSv2/DNS-rebind detail)
action: Read packs/strix/skills-internal/vulnerabilities/<class>.md verbatim — descriptive+underscored filenames (sql_injection.md, authentication_jwt.md, path_traversal_lfi_rfi.md, race_conditions.md, llm_prompt_injection.md, agentic_system_security.md). Not every class has one — ls the dir

name: Extract PayloadsAllTheThings class dir on-demand
precondition: brain/payloads/<class>.txt is thin (<50 lines) OR the vuln class is exotic/legacy (SSI, XPath injection, LaTeX injection, LDAP injection variants)
action: tar -xzf packs/payloads-all-the-things/pat-full.tar.gz -C /tmp/pat --wildcards '*<class>*' && ls /tmp/pat/ then grep the extracted README for payloads. 48 existing brain/lessons.md attributions confirm this pack is the canonical fallback

name: Dispatch browser-stealth-agent for CF-protected targets
precondition: Target returns cf-ray / Cloudflare interstitial / Akamai bot challenge / Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise / DataDome / PerimeterX / Turnstile widget on vanilla probes
action: 1. Ensure camofox-browser is running: curl -sSf http://localhost:9377/health >/dev/null || (cd packs/camofox-browser && nohup npm start > /tmp/camofox.log 2>&1 &) 2. Dispatch browser-stealth-agent for stealth recon + evidence capture. Complementary to PAT-cr-01 (CloudRip origin-IP scan) — run both, they attack different CF mechanisms

name: Dispatch browser-verifier for every reflected/stored/DOM XSS finding
precondition: XSS finding based on curl reflection or Burp response — proof of EXECUTION (not just reflection) not yet captured
action: Dispatch browser-verifier. Reflection != execution — ~90% of curl-reflected XSS fails in browser (CSP blocks, framework auto-escape, DOM ≠ HTML, encoding, wrong context, browser-only WAF). Uses camofox-browser (packs/camofox-browser/) for consistency across CF-protected and unprotected targets. 4-tier detection ladder: dialog → DOM marker → OOB (fetch/sendBeacon/preload) → all-three-negative before BROWSER_REJECTED

name: AI-gateway attack surface enumeration + quota/routing bypass
precondition: Target detected as AI-gateway — multi-provider LLM routing, /dashboard/free-tiers or similar quota view, /mcp or /a2a endpoints, /api/providers, /api/keys, per-provider dashboards
action: 1. Enumerate providers via /api/providers or dashboard scrape 2. Test cross-provider quota bypass (spoof x-provider-hint, tenant-id, session cookie) 3. Test prompt-routing bypass (force expensive-model path via model= param override or header injection) 4. Credential-vault IDOR on /api/keys/{id} and /api/providers/{id}/keys 5. MCP/A2A auth confusion — call /mcp/tools/list with A2A scope token or vice versa 6. Dashboard tenant IDOR on /dashboard/free-tiers?tenant= 7. Cost-accounting race — parallel bursts to see if quota decrement is transactional. Chain: quota bypass → free LLM abuse; credential IDOR → provider-key exfil → billing fraud on victim's account
